newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Israel's Netanyahu, angered by charges, seeks talks.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Netanyahu, angered by charges, seeks talks.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Wednesday he was "fed up" with accusations that Israeli actions were hurting the chances of peace in the Middle East and called for direct Israeli-Palestinian contacts.

"I'm getting, frankly, fed up with the idea that everything we do is a violation of the (peace) agreement, and everything the Palestinians say is in compliance with the agreement," he told a news conference at the end of a visit to Moscow.

The remarks coincide with renewed tension between Israel and Palestinians and mounting international diplomatic pressure on Israel since Netanyahu approved plans to build Jewish housing in Arab East Jerusalem.

Netanyahu said Palestinians should address any problems they have in the peace process directly to Israel, an apparent reference to a proposal on Tuesday by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat to convene U.S., European and Arab envoys at a meeting on Saturday.
"If the Palestinians are serious about peace, let them sit down with us. If they are serious about airing their differences, let them sit down with us," Netanyahu said.

"We want real peace partners...peace in which we talk to one another, peace in which we address one another, peace in which we don't shut down the telephones, peace in which we don't engage in histrionics."

Arafat refused to answer two telephone calls from Netanyahu on Monday, Israeli television reported. A PLO official said Arafat had refused more than twice since Friday to receive Netanyahu's representatives.
U.S. officials in Washington said that, if invited, they would attend Arafat's proposed meeting of envoys.
"Chairman Arafat obviously feels the need to talk to friendly countries around the world, and that's appropriate," U.S. State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns said on Tuesday.
Netanyahu expressed frustration with the international pressure.
"A few months ago we were accused of burrowing a tunnel under the Al Aksa Mosque - preposterous fabrication!" Netanyahu said, referring to the sacred mosque in Jerusalem.

"It should have been thrown out by the international community, thrown out by the international press. It was given credence, this lie," he said. "I'm not going to accept this same kind of approach again and again."
Jordan's King Hussein, the Arab leader closest to Netanyahu, warned the Israeli prime minister of an "explosion of the peace process" unless the Jerusalem settlement plan was dropped.
But Netanyahu said during his Moscow trip that Israel's recent moves did not threaten the Middle East peace process.
"This kind of doomsday talk and the whole histrionic attitude towards obvious disagreement is itself not conducive to the (peace) process," he told reporters on Tuesday.
"We have disagreements. We cannot at every stage of this agreement engage in cataclysmic predictions and talk of crisis and violence."
Violence has erupted around Hebron in recent days.

An Israeli soldier guarding a West Bank Jewish settlement near Hebron was stabbed 20 times and wounded seriously in an apparent Palestinian guerrilla attack, Israeli military sources said on Tuesday. At least 10 Palestinians were injured in clashes with Israeli soldiers near Hebron on Monday.

"If they think that they can foment violence, increase tension and send oblique but readily understandable signals that they will foment quote spontaneous violence, we're not going to play that game," Netanyahu said.
